}}'''Dame Julia Mary Goodfellow''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|DBE|FMedSci|FInstP}} (née '''Lansdall'''; born 1 July 1951) is a former [[Vice-Chancellor]] of the [[University of Kent]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kent.ac.uk/news/stories/dbeforvc/2010 |title=University of Kent website, 1 |access-date=2010-08-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110609183218/http://www.kent.ac.uk/news/stories/dbeforvc/2010 |archive-date=2011-06-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kent.ac.uk/news/inthenews/june/24.html |title=University of Kent website, 2 |access-date=2010-08-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402121352/http://www.kent.ac.uk/news/inthenews/june/24.html |archive-date=2015-04-02 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.bbk.ac.uk/about_us/fellows/goodfellow Birkbeck College website]</ref> and Chair of the [[British Science Association]].<ref>[http://www.britishscienceassociation.org/british-science-association/council British Science Association Council] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130606081021/http://www.britishscienceassociation.org/british-science-association/council |date=2013-06-06 }}</ref> She was the president of [[Universities UK]] from 1 August 2015 until July 2017.<ref name="UUK">{{cite web|title=Professor Dame Julia Goodfellow elected President of Universities UK for 2015 - 2017|url=http://www.universitiesuk.ac.uk/highereducation/Pages/ProfessorDameJuliaGoodfellowelectedPresidentofUniversitiesUKfor2015-2017.aspx#.|publisher=UUK|access-date=1 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002040150/http://www.universitiesuk.ac.uk/highereducation/Pages/ProfessorDameJuliaGoodfellowelectedPresidentofUniversitiesUKfor2015-2017.aspx#.|archive-date=2 October 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="THES">{{cite news|last1=Morgan|first1=John|title=Julia Goodfellow to be first female UUK president|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/news/julia-goodfellow-to-be-first-female-uuk-president/2017243.article|access-date=1 August 2015|work=timeshighereducation.co.uk|date=27 November 2014}}</ref>

==Early life, education and career==
Goodfellow completed her [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] degree in physics at the [[University of Bristol]]<ref name="goodfellowBSc">[http://www.bristol.ac.uk/alumni/featured/science/index.html Faculty of Science: Alumni and friends] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140820013404/http://www.bristol.ac.uk/alumni/featured/science/index.html |date=2014-08-20 }}, bristol.ac.uk; accessed 9 April 2016.</ref>  and obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in biophysics at the [[Open University]]<ref name="goodfellowphd">{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|first=Julia|last=Goodfellow|title=Structural studies of the corneal stroma|publisher=Open University|date=1975|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.456973|authorlink=Julia Goodfellow}}</ref> Research Unit in [[Oxford]]. She began her career as Professor of Biomolecular Science at [[Birkbeck College]] in 1995, and was promoted to Vice Master in 1998.<ref>[http://www.kent.ac.uk/vicechancellor/profile.html Goodfellow profile at the University of Kent website]</ref> In 2002, she was appointed chief executive of the [[Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council]], the first woman to lead a UK research council.<ref name="THES"/> Goodfellow served as chair of the [[British Science Association]] from 2009 to 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=David Willetts to be new chair of the BSA|publisher=British Science Association|url=http://www.britishscienceassociation.org/News/former-science-minister-david-willetts-to-be-new-chair-of-the-british-science-association|access-date=7 October 2015}}</ref>

In 2007, she was appointed Vice-Chancellor of the University of Kent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kentonline.co.uk/canterbury/news/university-appoints-new-vice-cha-a29035/|website=Kent Online News|title=University appoints new vice-chancellor|access-date=28 September 2015|date=2007-04-02}}</ref> In 2011, she was appointed to both the [[Council for Science and Technology]] and the [[Science and Technology Facilities Council]].<ref name="UUK"/> Currently, Goodfellow is a member of the Higher Education Policy Institute (Hepi) advisory board.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hepi.ac.uk/about-us/who-we-are/advisory-board|title=Advisory Board|website=Higher Education Policy Institute (Hepi)|access-date=28 September 2015}}</ref>

Goodfellow was elected [[Universities UK]] president from 2015 to 2017, the first woman to hold the role. In 2015 Goodfellow stated that Universities UK supported staying in the [[European Union]], citing the “economic growth, employable graduates and cutting edge research discoveries” that the EU could provide in the education sector.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thepienews.com/news/universities-uk-declares-in-stance-in-uks-eu-debate/n|title=Universities UK declares "in" stance in UK's EU debate|publisher=The PIE News|access-date=5 October 2015}}</ref> In 2018 she became president of the [[Royal Society of Biology]].<ref>The Biologist 65(2) p22-25</ref>

==Honours==
*2001: Appointed [[Order of the British Empire|Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE)
*2002: Honorary [[Doctor of Science]] (Hon DSc) degree from the University of Bristol<ref>[http://www.bristol.ac.uk/news/2002/hondegsjun.html Honorary degrees at Bristol University], bristol.ac.uk; accessed 9 April 2016.</ref>
*2002: Honorary Doctor of Science degree from the [[University of Strathclyde]]<ref name="goodfellowBSc"/>
*2004: [[Doctor of the University]] (DUniv) degree from the [[University of Essex]]<ref>[http://www.essex.ac.uk/honorary_graduates/or/2004/julia-goodfellow-oration.aspx Honorary Graduates], essex.ac.uk; accessed 9 April 2016.</ref>
*2005: Honorary Doctor of Science degree from the [[University of Edinburgh]]<ref>[http://www.ed.ac.uk/about/people/honorary-degrees/2004-5 Honorary graduates 2004-05] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141202160937/http://www.ed.ac.uk/about/people/honorary-degrees/2004-5 |date=2014-12-02 }}, ed.ac.uk; accessed 9 April 2016.</ref>
*2005: Honorary Doctor of Science degree from [[Durham University]]<ref>[https://www.dur.ac.uk/news/newsitem/?itemno=3821 News: Six set for honorary doctorates at Durham University], dur.ac.uk; accessed 9 April 2016.</ref>
*2009: Honorary Doctor of Science degree from the [[University of Manchester]]<ref>[http://www.manchester.ac.uk/discover/news/article/?id=5142 Quartet to be honoured at Manchester], manchester.ac.uk; accessed 9 April 2016.</ref>
*2010: Promoted to [[Order of the British Empire|Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (DBE) 'For services to Science'<ref name="LG 12 June 2010">{{London Gazette|issue=59446|date=12 June 2010|page=6|supp=y}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 1972, Julia Lansdall married [[Peter Goodfellow (geneticist)|Peter Goodfellow]], with whom she has one daughter and one son.{{citation needed|date=April 2016}}

==Criticism==
Goodfellow has been criticised for her travel expenses and pay for the 2014-15 year. Her travel expenses were reported to be £26,635, with 92% of flights being first or business class. She also received a pay rise of 3% in the same year, increasing her salary to £272,000.<ref>Florence Maher, [http://thetab.com/uk/kent/2016/02/12/ukc-vc-spent-incredible-26635-flying-first-class-last-year-8456 UKC VC spent a staggering £26,635 on flying first class last year], thetab.com; accessed 9 April 2016.</ref>

She received a £43,000 pay rise in 2012–13, a rise of 19%.<ref name="kentonline.co.uk">[http://www.kentonline.co.uk/canterbury/news/pay-rise-puts-university-boss-33387 University of Kent vice-chancellor Professor Dame Julia Goodfellow's salary increases to £265,000], kentonline.co.uk; accessed 9 April 2016.</ref> Other staff at the university were striking to secure a 2% pay rise in the same year.<ref name="kentonline.co.uk"/> The university was criticised by the University and College Union for attempting to "obscure key information" by obfuscating records of the meeting in which her salary was decided.{{citation needed|date=April 2016}}
